entry.dc:title: Analysis of water level and land subsidence data from thorez open-pit mine, Hungary
entry.dc:creator: Jambrik R.
entry.dc:description: The most important occurrence of land subsidence in Hungary caused by underground water withdrawal can be found in the NE of Hungary, in an area of open-pit mining at the foot of the Matra mountains. This paper presents the monitoring system of the underground water withdrawal, the processing method of achieving the underground water depletion and of the land subsidence as its indirect effect, as well as conclusions which can be drawn from the analysis of the observed data. The back analysis is illustrated by examples. © 1995 Springer-Verlag.

entry.dc:title: Closure concerns at Sonora Mining's Jamestone Mine
entry.dc:creator: Dahlstrand A.
entry.dc:description: The mine's close proximity to the town of Jamestown has made it a highly visible operation. Due to its location and local opposition, the Jamestown operation and production schedule has been impacted by concerns related to noise, air quality, blasting water quality and wildlife. As a result, the Jamestown Mine built into its operations phase intensified efforts in monitoring, concurrent reclamation, wildlife buffers and a landscape-screening plan. Closing the open-pit mining operation has required resolution of numerous issues. Reclamation and closure involve environmental protection issues, community issues and people issues. The obvious and often most expensive of them is the physical reclamation of mining disturbance and the elimination and long-term commitments and maintenance. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Practical issues of geostatistical reserve estimation in the mining industry
entry.dc:creator: Guocheng Pan
entry.dc:description: Geostatistics has been widely accepted as a standard tool for reserve estimation and mine planning. Kriging has been adopted as the best estimator of grade. Although many discussions have been conducted in the use of kriging in the mining industry, insufficient attention has been given to solutions for over-smoothing. This study attempts to link over-smoothing effects with several other practical aspects in kriging. These include the weight independence of data values, variogram modeling, and search strategy used in estimation. All solutions recommended here are suited for precious metal deposits in open-pit mining. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Geologic and geochemical characteristics of the Yichun Ta-Nb-Li deposit, Jiangxi Province, south China
entry.dc:creator: Lin Yin
entry.dc:description: The Yichun Ta-Nb-Li mine is situated within a small, sheetlike body of topaz-lepidolite granite which is the most fractionated phase of the Yashan batholith. Volumetrically, the most important phase in the batholith is a coarse-grained, protolithionite-muscovite granite which has a finer grained, muscovite granite margin. The protolithionite-muscovite granite is intruded by small bodies of muscovite granite which form the locus of a tungsten vein system at the Xin Fang tungsten mine. Two sheetlike bodies, a lower Li mica granite and an upper topaz-lepidolite granite intrude the upper contact between the protolithionite-muscovite granite and the host metasediments. The granites are crosscut by unmineralized porphyry dikes that are exploited as a source of kaolin. The topaz-lepidolite granite is a major, low-grade Ta-Nb-Li deposit which is exploited via open-pit mining. The mineralogy and geochemistry of the ore deposits are described. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Towards the 30th anniversary of West-Siberian Iron and Steel Works
entry.dc:creator: Kustov B.
entry.dc:description: A review is made on development and advances of the West Siberian Iron and Steel Works since its inception. The Works pioneered in application of flame guniting for converter lining, thermal hardening of shaped sections from the rolling temperature, cast-iron melting with high-alumina and high-magnesia slags, coke production from the coal of open-pit mining. Among other things mixing ladles and blast-furnace chargers were mastered along with production of rolled metal, metal cord, alloy welding wire etc.

entry.dc:title: Geology and geochemistry of Summitville, Colorado: an epithermal acid sulfate deposit in a volcanic dome
entry.dc:creator: Gray J.
entry.dc:description: Geologic studies during recent open-pit mining at Summitville, Colorado, have provided new information on an epithermal acid sulfate Au-Ag-Cu deposit formed in a volcanic dome. Geologic mapping, geochemical studies of whole-rock samples from blast holes, and geologic and geochemical traverse studies refine the details of the evolution of the Summitville deposit. Six distinct events followed emplacement of the quartz latite volcanic dome and define the development of the Summitville deposit: 1) an early stage of acid sulfate alteration, 2) subsequent Cu sulfide and gold mineralization, 3) widespread hydrothermal brecciation, 4) volumetrically minor, base metal sulfide-bearing barite veining, 5) volumetrically minor, kaolinite matrix brecciation, and finally, 6) supergene oxidation. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Computerized mine planning for medium-size open-pits
entry.dc:creator: Blackwell G.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
entry.dc:description: Sequences in open-pit mining must be planned and regularly revised to incorporate changes in the variables that affect profitability. Interactive computer planning with colour graphic facilities is an effective tool for this purpose in the short and medium term. Hardware for such purposes, in the form of personal computers, is readily available, and the techniques have been shown to contribute significantly to planning effectiveness and profitability. Successful planning requires skilled personnel who are familiar with all aspects of mine operations and related matters. Their decisions can be input into expert-system databases to educate and assist less experienced personnel. Within limits fluctuations in well-defined, short-term grades can be smoothed by using linear programming to adjust the mining sequence. In the longer term the lack of sampling data precludes detailed planning, and broad adjustments to monthly or quarterly sequences are required to ensure a continuously developing, practical mine plan.

entry.dc:title: Computer-based optimization of open-pit mining sequences
entry.dc:creator: Huang S.
entry.prism:publicationName: Transactions of the Institution of Mining and Metallurgy Section A Mining Technology
entry.dc:description: An interactive model and corresponding computer software for optimization of the open-pit mining sequence have been developed at the Institute of Mining Engineering, Technical University of Berlin. The model is supported by graphics software and consists of three linear programming systems and a simulation module. With this model an optimum mining sequence for a multi-level open-pit mine can be determined under a criterion selected by the planner.

entry.dc:title: Stratigraphic evidence of a pre-wisconsinan interglaciation in the Adirondack Mountains, New York
entry.dc:creator: Muller E.
entry.dc:description: Multiple tills separated by interbedded lake sediments were temporarily exposed during open-pit mining at Sanford Hill, near Newcomb, in the central Adirondack Mountains of northeastern New York. Radiocarbon ages of wood fragments from brown clay between two tills at that site indicate an age older than 55,000 yr B.P. A pollen profile in the brown pond clay (Tahawus clay) records a transition from initial domination by pine, spruce, and birch to an oak pollen zone. The upward disappearance of spruce and decrease of pine and birch are accompanied by diversification and increase in hardwood pollen. This assemblage includes several warm-climate hardwood species that are not represented in the postglacial flora of the region, suggesting that the biota existed during an interglacial or interstadial interval that was warmer and/or longer than postglacial time. Accordingly, the Tahawus clay is tentatively assigned to the Sangamon interglaciation, and probably to marine oxygen isotope substage 5e. Truncation of the Tahawus clay by glacial erosion may account for the absence of a Sangamon paleosol. © 1993 University of Washington.

entry.dc:title: Acquisition and signal processing of ground-penetrating radar for shallow exploration and open-pit mining
entry.dc:creator: Baker P.
entry.dc:description: The Australian Mineral Industries Research Association (AMIRA) has sponsored Monash University to investigate the acquisition and signal processing of ground-penetrating radar (GPR) for shallow exploration and open-pit mining. This project had three objectives: (1) to acquire high-quality GPR data sets for shallow exploration and surface mining applications under a variety of geological conditions; (2) to develop signal-processing techniques to enhance radar profiles prior to detailed interpretation; (3) to assess the accuracy of GPR and associated processing techniques through comparisons with independent measurements. Over one hundred kilometres of data were recorded at the various sponsors sites in a wide variety of geological conditions for different economic targets. Several examples are presented to demonstrate: 1) the hand-carried and vehicle-towed acquisition techniques, 2) target detection at depths down to 25 m, 3) the benefits of signal processing for good and poor quality data, 4) the use of dielectric measurements, petrophysical modelling and frequency-dependent synthetic radargrams, 5) the application of seismic interpretation concepts. The project has demonstrated commercially acceptable rates of GPR data acquisition where the penetration is satisfactory. Some of the unfavourable Australian geological conditions for radar have also been identified. Although signal processing techniques have extended the applicable range of the radar technique, additional hardware enhancements have been identified to improve the commercial application of radar. The next stage is to assess the economic feasibility of radar by comparison with competing techniques such as drilling. © ASEG 1992.

entry.dc:title: On a number of spare haulage units for the shovel-truck system in open pit mines
entry.dc:creator: Czaplicki J.M.
entry.prism:publicationName: International Journal of Surface Mining Reclamation and Environment
entry.dc:description: Shovel-truck systems are widely applied in open-pit mining. In these systems spare haulage units are employed as a rule. Recommendations and rules which are used to determine the reserve truck fleet size can give significant difference in estimation of a number of units needed for a given system. The paper consider the problem of proper selection of a spare haulage unit fleet size taking into account economical and technical parameters of trucks, their exploitation process as well as the reliability indices. © 1992, Taylor & Francis Group, LLC. All rights reserved.

entry.dc:title: Structure and age of the Cerro de Pasco Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag deposit, Peru
entry.dc:creator: Cheney E.
entry.dc:description: The world-famous Cu-Zn-Pb-Ag deposit at Cerro de Pasco, Peru, consists of texturally massive pyrite, texturally massive sphalerite-galena-pyrite, and veins containing pyrite and enargite. Historically the deposit has been considered to be the hydrothermal product of the adjacent Miocene volcanic and intrusive complex (locally known as the "Vent"). However, both the texturally massive sulfides of the deposit and the pre-Miocene strata are cut by the Longitudinal fault, one of the largest faults in the district, but the Vent is not. Imbrication by the Longitudinal fault zone (duplex structures) has thickened the deposit so that it is amenable to open-pit mining. Dikes and pyrite-enargite veins pass from the Vent into the massive sulfides; fragments of massive pyrite occur in the Vent. Thus, no matter what their origin, the texturally massive sulfides are older and, therefore, genetically unrelated to the Vent. © 1991 Springer-Verlag.

entry.dc:title: German reunification brings cleanup tasks
entry.dc:creator: Michel J.
entry.prism:publicationName: Forum for Applied Research Public Policy
entry.dc:description: Among the recently freed communist nations of Eastern Europe, East Germany probably was the most prosperous. It had the highest gross percapita income and was self-sufficient in food, energy, and most manufactured goods, yet by Western standards, East Germany's economy was fragile. Since reunification, much of its industry has been shut down because of inefficiencies, and unemployment could reach 50% of the work force. This paper details the grave environmental abuses that accompanied East Germany's former prosperity and that today present a united Germany with a massive cleanup chore. In energy, for example, extensive open-pit mining and burning of lignite - the primary energy source for the former republic - created major problems in land use, water quality, and air pollution control. Of particular concern is the high levels of sulfur dioxide emissions that need to be reduced by 1993 to meet treaty obligations. Pollution levels, closely guarded under the communist regime, are believed responsible for damage to 65% of East Germany's forests. Among other major environmental problems are contaminated tap water, toxic waste discharges from chemical plants, "wild' garbage dumps, and traffic congestion. -from Author

entry.dc:title: Extraction of non-traditional types of hydrocarbon resources by application of electromagnetic energy
entry.dc:creator: Makogon Y.F.
entry.dc:description: Recently, there is a significant interest in prospecting for and developing non-traditional types of hydrocarbon resources, as petroleum bitumens, gas hydrates, oil shales, and ozokerite. Significant reserves of such resources exist, and they constitute an energy and raw-materials alternative to oil and gas. Also, natural bitumens contain significant quantities of valuable minerals and compounds. Under formation conditions, these alternative hydrocarbon-containing substances completely fill the pore space and exist in solid, crystalline or amorphous state. Their extraction by familiar oil-and-gas production techniques is therefore impossible. There is a need for new techniques of hydrocarbons extraction by open-pit mining and in wells. One such method involves the application of electromagnetic energy, which is injected into the formation in the form of high-frequency electromagnetic waves. The interaction of electromagnetic waves with the rocks generates heat sources and ponderommotive forces and physicochemical surface phenomena, electrocapillary and electrosurface effects which could be useful in their production.

entry.dc:title: A methodology for the optimum control of shovel and truck operations in open-pit mining
entry.dc:creator: Li Z.
entry.dc:description: This paper presents a methodology for the optimum control of shovel and truck operations in open-pit mining. Particularly discussed are the problems of material flow planning, truck dispatching, and equipment matching. The linear programming technique is used for planning material flows along paths in the haulage network, the maximum intertruck-time deviation rule of truck dispatching is proposed for facilitating implementation of automated truck dispatching systems, and the least square of intertruck-time deviation is suggested as the criterion for optimally matching trucks with shovels. © 1990 Elsevier Science Publishers B.V.

entry.dc:title: The Industrial Landscape of Rio Tinto, Huelva, Spain
entry.dc:creator: Willies L.
entry.dc:description: Rio Tinto has the largest deposits of pyrite and copper pyrite and associated minerals in Europe. It was exploited by the pre-Roman Iberians for silver and copper, and later by the Romans. The greatest change to the landscape came with open-pit mining or quarrying by the British Rio Tinto Company in the late nineteenth century and the first half of the twentieth century for pyrite for sulphur and copper. Even this will be obliterated by current mining projects — the Cerro Colorado project of 1973 was started by the Spanish successor company, Rio Tinto Minera (though still associated with the RTZ multi-national company), and more recently there has been an intensification of gold and silver extraction from the gossan which overlies the pyritic deposits. Damage to the industrial archaeology is also resulting from a large scale reclamation programme, and an attempt to develop a Museum Park on the site largely failed. This report briefly considers the remains at Rio Tinto, and includes photographs recording pre-1950 features of the mines. © 1989 Maney Publishing.

entry.dc:title: Geology of the Vulture mine
entry.dc:creator: White D.
entry.dc:description: The Vulture mine near Wickenburg, Arizona was a major gold producer from 1863 to 1942, having yielded about 11t(12.1 st) Au and 8t(8.8st) Ag. Gold occurs as coarse native metal and electrum in quartz veins and also finely disseminated within a quartz monzonite sill and its silicified wall rock. The sill is semi-conformable within a Proterozoic volcaniclastic-dominated sequence, all dipping north about 35°. Early mining focused on the vein-hosted gold, particularly in the immediate hanging wall and footwall of the sill. Later efforts included some open-pit mining of the outcropping sill and adjacent altered and mineralized rock. Two sets of post-mineral faults have complicated the orebody geometry. The Proterozoic rocks are notably lean in precious metals except where altered in proximity to the Creataceous stock and still. Circumstances dictate an interpretation of epigenetic mineralization related to the Laramide intrusion.

entry.dc:title: Dumping of other than mining waste in mining cavities - Basic legal and mine-engineering conditions
entry.dc:creator: Furer G.
entry.dc:description: The amount of waste produced by an industrial and consumer society such as that of the Federal Republic of Germany is enormous. A vital objective of legislation is to avoid and recycle wastes, but this is still in the initial stages. Consequently, many waste materials with ecologically objectionable properties must be eliminated at geologically and hydrologically suitable disposal sites. Such dumps include cavities resulted from mining activities, such as open-pit mining, underground mining, and caverns produced by leaching. The general legal as well as technical waste-disposal and mining conditions which currently have to be satisfied in the Federal Republic of Germany are discussed.

entry.dc:title: Influence of blasting techniques on open pit economics
entry.dc:creator: Singhal R.K.
entry.dc:description: The economics of open-pit mining depend heavily on the cost of overburden removal. It is necessary to maintain a pit slope as steep as possible. Several factors affect the stability of pitwalls. This article deals with one such controllable factor - drilling and blasting. The economics of steeper pit slopes is discussed, followed by a record of drilling and blasting practices in western Canadian surface mines. Microprocessor-based instrumentation and its application to blasthole drilling is also described.

entry.dc:title: Development of a route determination system on open-pit mining using personal computer
entry.dc:creator: Hagiwara Y.
entry.prism:publicationName: Waseda Daigaku Rikogaku Kenkyusho Hokoku Bulletin of Science and Engineering Research Laboratory Waseda University
entry.dc:description: The authors have developed a haul road determination system for shovel and dump truck method hauling on open-pit mining sites. Under this system, the optimum haul road (or route) should provide the highest possible safety to the travelling dump truck as well as the shortest possible cycle time. Uncertain conditions and indefinite factors inherent to designing an open-pit mine have been simplified in order to put a personal computer into practical use. A simulation test has revealed that the use of this system has practical value up to 80 × 80 mesh data by translating BASIC to ASSEMBLER language.

entry.dc:title: Development work continues for open-pit mining at Red Dog
entry.dc:creator: Hodgson S.
entry.dc:description: The Red Dog zinc/lead deposit in northwest Alaska is the second largest zinc deposit ever discovered. Being developed by Caminco Alaska, with startup scheduled for early 1990, it will ultimately be the largest zinc mine in the Western World. The article describes proposed mining operations and ore treatment. The partnership between Cominco and NANA is unique. It is the first major resource development in Alaska in which a native corporation has had direct participation.

entry.dc:title: USE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE METHODS IN OPEN-PIT MINING.
entry.dc:creator: Brfueggemann H.
entry.dc:description: This article is based on a specific application of open-pit mining - the exploitation of raw material for cement production - but its validity is not restricted to this domain. In recent years Krupp Polysius has established a software package for the computation of numerical deposit models, based on borehole samples and topograpical data. Subsequently an additional module was required to evaluate these models and deduce a suitable mining strategy, taking into consideration different constraining factors related to the process technology. All work was performed within the framework of a real, normal-scale example, but all concepts, designs and finished software components are set up to deal with general open pit mining applications - they are not restricted to this specific application.

entry.dc:title: Finite element modeling of the Rurscholle multi-aquifer groundwater system
entry.dc:creator: Dorgarten H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Computational Methods in Water Resources Vol 1 Proc 7th Conference Cambridge Ma 1988
entry.dc:description: In order to simulate the impact of open-pit mining, a complex finite element multi-aquifer groundwater model was developed. Special algorithms were included to describe the progressing excavation and refilling of the pits. As the groundwater drawdown causes both wide-ranging depressions and steep gradients, extended project-areas and relatively small elements are required, resulting in extremely large meshes. Thus, simulations can only be performed by highly vectorized models on today's super-computers. -from Author

entry.dc:title: The discovery of the Brouzils antimony deposit in the Vendee, Massif Armoricain, France: prospection, description of deposit, proposed exploitation
entry.dc:creator: Le Fur Y.
entry.dc:description: The country rocks of the veins are Lower Palaeozoic greywackes and grey to green shales with intervals of volcanic material. The have been deformed during the Early Devonian and Late Devonian/Early Carboniferous (Bretonian), with the formation of N100° to N135° trending folds accompanied by schistosity, and of shears and slides of the same trend. They have also been affected by N-S, E-W and NE-SW extension and fracturing. The Vendee antimony vein field was detected by bedrock Sb geochemistry and electromagnetic survey, followed by trenching and drilling. The veins, including those of Rochetrejoux and Brouzils, occupy tension gashes and shear fractures related to major phases of activity of the South Armorican faults. The vein field developed at the intersection of two fracture systems and includes N-S structures recognised discontinuously over distances of 2-3km, and a main NE-SW bundle dipping NE at 75°-80°. This structure is 6-7m wide and has been recognised over a length of 800m and down to depths of 50-100m. Five richer columns ranging from 30 to 120m long have been distinguished within the bundle. Chalcedonic quartz and stibnite in variable proportions are the main vein-filling minerals, with very minor carbonates, pyrite and arsenopyrite. The geological reserves are estimated at 6000 t of Sb metal, of which 3000 t can be extracted by open-pit mining, in an ore containing 6-7% Sb. The ore can be processed to give excellent commercial concentrate with no impurities or penalising elements. The Gagneraud-BRGM mining project involves open-cast mining of the first 20m at a rate of 100 t Sb per month, protecting the deeper levels. -from English summary
